classification.difficultyReason: Compare shaded areas, including half-cells and unequal visible regions, and simplify the represented fraction.

content.prompt: Which of these shows exactly two thirds?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, first pattern from the left
spec.description: A three-by-three square grid with six complete shaded cells and two shaded half-cells.
spec.mathematics: Shaded area is 7/9 of the square.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied shaded pattern is visible; its fraction and correctness are not printed.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, second pattern from the left
spec.description: A three-by-three grid with the top-middle cell, middle-middle cell and entire bottom row shaded, plus the lower triangles of the two outer middle-row cells.
spec.mathematics: Five complete cells and two half-cells give 6/9 = 2/3.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied shaded pattern is visible; no correctness mark or answer appears in the question figure.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, third pattern from the left
spec.description: A three-by-three grid with a shaded cross and four unshaded corner cells.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied shading is visible; the fraction is withheld.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, fourth pattern from the left
spec.description: Three equal-width columns and three principal rows. The right column is shaded. In the first two columns, only the upper half of the top row and lower half of the bottom row are shaded.
spec.mathematics: The shaded area equals five principal cells out of nine; unequal visible cell sizes must be retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no fraction or correctness mark is supplied.

answer.worked:
The two shaded half-cells make one whole cell, so the second pattern has the area of 6 shaded cells out of 9.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{6}{9}&=\frac{6\div3}{9\div3}\\&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: Second pattern.
